thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 - high error rate on /v1/generate in production (us-west). Alert: 5xx spike, latency > 3s for 95th percentile. Triggered at 2026-03-15T02:12:01Z.

mike: I'm looking. dashboard shows a sudden drop in token throughput and queue length spiking on runtime-cluster-3.

sophia: I'm pulling logs for the runtime pods. Any customer-impacting calls? which plans?

olivia: Grafana shows most errors are downstream timeouts from the serving runtime to the kv-cache (redis). Errors concentrated on 10.10.14.* nodes. Two large customers (acme-inc, shoply) have elevated error rates.

mike: Paging infra: nate, any active infra deploys in us-west?

nate: No deploys. We had a maintenance reboot on node pool yesterday but health checks passed. Looks like a sudden backend timeout regression since 02:10.

sophia: Ok quick mitigations proposal: 1) enable shedding for low-tier plans (reduce in-flight for those requests), 2) reduce runtime request timeout to 15s from 30s, 3) set max_in_flight per runtime from 200 -> 80 to reduce head-of-line blocking, 4) temporarily tighten per-customer rate limits for acme-inc/shoply. Thoughts?

mike: +1 on shedding + timeout. We should also enable queueing limit (500) to avoid unlimited backlog. Do we have a safe command to change these live?

devops-bot: Runbook snippet: use rtctl to update runtime config. Example:
```
# set max in-flight
rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key max_in_flight --value 80
# enable shedding for plan:free and plan:starter
rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key enable_shedding_plans --value "free,starter"
# set request timeout
rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key request_timeout_s --value 15
# set queue capacity
rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key queue_capacity --value 500
```

mike: I'm running the first two now. Pasting outputs.

mike: ```
$ rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key max_in_flight --value 80
OK: config applied to 12/12 runtime pods (rolling restart)
$ rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key enable_shedding_plans --value "free,starter"
OK: shedding enabled for plans: free,starter
```

sophia: I'll change the timeout and queue next. Applying with care to avoid mass restarts.

sophia: ```
$ rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key request_timeout_s --value 15 --no-restart
OK: live config updated
$ rtctl update-config --cluster runtime-cluster-3 --key queue_capacity --value 500 --no-restart
OK: queue capacity set to 500
```

olivia: After those changes, 95th p95 latency dropped from ~4.2s to ~1.6s within 90s. Error rate for /v1/generate decreased from 8% -> 1.2% across the cluster.

nate: For acme-inc and shoply I temporarily applied a stricter per-key rate limit to prevent them from overwhelming the degraded backend. Command: `admin-api patch /keys/{key}/rate-limit {"qps": 3}`. Both customers are within a retry window.

mike: Notifying support to communicate to acme-inc/shoply (they may see throttling). Olivia, can you cold-start a canary slot with the fallback model (smaller quantized variant) as an extra fallback?

olivia: Starting canary on runtime-cluster-3-slot-b. Command: `deploy-tool canary --model rwd-small-q4 --slot slot-b --cluster runtime-cluster-3`

devops-bot: Canary deploy started. Health checks pending.

sophia: Observability note: enable detailed traces for 10% of requests to diagnose kv-cache timeouts. `tracing.set_sample_rate(cluster=runtime-cluster-3,rate=0.1)`

mike: I'm going to handoff in 30m. oncall-rotation: handing over to @sophia for the remainder of the incident. I will be reachable if it resurfaces.

oncall-rotation: mike -> sophia : primary on-call handoff acknowledged.

sophia: Accepted. Current mitigation summary to attach to incident ticket:
- Applied max_in_flight=80 (reduces concurrency to avoid H-O-L)
- Enabled shedding for free/starter plans
- Reduced request_timeout_s=15s to fail fast and free KV connections
- Queue capacity limited to 500 to bound memory pressure
- Tightened per-key QPS for top noisy customers (acme-inc, shoply)
- Canary fallback model deployed in slot-b
- Tracing sample rate 10% for deeper analysis

sophia: Next action items: 1) investigate root cause of kv-cache latency spike (redis cluster metrics + network), 2) evaluate whether to re-balance traffic across us-east, 3) create post-incident load test to reproduce.

olivia: Support pinged acme-inc with temporary throttling notice. They acknowledged - asked for ETA. I said ~2 hours while we stabilize.

nate: I see elevated retries on egress network links to redis shard 7. Running `tcpdump` and redis slowlog capture now. If it's network flapping, we may need to drain that host.

sophia: Good. Keep this thread updated. I'll escalate to infra if we confirm host-level networking. If metrics stay stable for 15m, plan is to gradually relax max_in_flight to 120 and widen queue to 1000.

mike: Thanks team. Leaving notes on the incident ticket with timestamps of each mitigation step.

incident-bot: Incident P0 acknowledged. Current status: mitigated (partial). Next update due in 15m or when state changes.
